claims: Diego Garcia is a joint U.S.-U.K. military base located on an atoll in the British Indian Ocean Territory.
Diego Garcia is known as the "Footprint of Freedom".
Diego Garcia serves as a hub for U.S. bomber missions, nuclear submarines, and naval operations in the Middle East and Indo-Pacific.
Diego Garcia is the southernmost and largest island of the Chagos Archipelago in the central Indian Ocean.
Diego Garcia is about 1,000 miles south of India.
Diego Garcia is a horseshoe-shaped atoll measuring roughly 40 miles in perimeter.
Diego Garcia encloses a deep lagoon.
Maximum elevations on Diego Garcia are often only a few feet above sea level.
The Diego Garcia base features an 8,000-foot-plus runway.
The runway at the Diego Garcia base supports B-1, B-2, and B-52 bombers.
The Diego Garcia base has a deep-draft port for aircraft carriers and nuclear submarines.
Diego Garcia was used for operations in the Middle East including Afghanistan and Iraq.
Diego Garcia was used for security in the South China Sea.
Approximately 2,400-5,000 people reside at Diego Garcia.
Residents at Diego Garcia include U.S. military personnel, DOD civilians, and civilian contractors.
Diego Garcia acts as a surveillance hub.
Diego Garcia acts as a satellite tracking hub for GPS.
Diego Garcia acts as a logistics hub.
In 2025, the UK agreed to transfer sovereignty to Mauritius while retaining a 99-year lease to maintain the Diego Garcia base.
In the 1970s, the UK forcibly removed the native Chagossian population to establish the Diego Garcia facility.
In March 2026, the Diego Garcia base was targeted in a failed ballistic missile attack, as described by The Times of India and The Jerusalem Post.
